title: Electronics for Technology
description: This course is an introduction to electricity and electronic devices. Students learn the basic theory of electricity and apply that knowledge to build, test, and troubleshoot electrical circuits. In the lab students learn to operate the test and measurement instrumentation necessary to support construction of electrical circuits.
outcomes: Describe the relationship of electric charge, current and electrical potential, and define the parameters which affect their value.
Explain the behavior of conductors, insulators, and semiconducting materials using the atomic model.
Demonstrate the transient and steady state behavior of the basic passive electrical components--resistors, capacitors, and inductors for both Alternating and Direct Current Inputs.
Identify the function of various electrical test and measurement equipment.
Apply Ohm's Law, Kirchoff's Law, Thevenin's Theorem, the Law of Circuit Superpositon, and other circuit analysis techniques to calculate circuit parameters.
